Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Leah Martinez (CTO - Nimbus), Omar Khan (Principal ML Eng - Nimbus), Priya Singh (Platform Eng - Nimbus)

Notes: Discovery focused on PLG/self-serve quickstart, hosted vs dedicated vs private, and pilot evaluation criteria. Shared artifacts: quickstart link, security deck, and benchmark template.
summary: Initial discovery for quickstart + pilot. Nimbus is evaluating Redwood hosted API for quick time-to-first-token but wants options for Dedicated/Private for production (data residency and compliance). Key concerns: latency, cost, SOC2/KMS, SSO, and ability to run benchmarks with their prompt set. Redwood AE/SE outlined free credits, quickstart flow, sample SDKs, and dedicated/private deployment tradeoffs.
transcript:
[00:00] Sasha: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, this is Sasha from Redwood. Quick intro from our side — Marco is our SE who will do the deep technical bits.
[00:15] Leah: Thanks Sasha. I can hear you. Quick intros from Nimbus: I'm Leah, CTO, Omar runs infra and ML, Priya handles platform.
[00:30] Marco: Nice to meet you all. Sasha, do you want to kick off with goals?
[00:35] Sasha: Yep, main goal today is to understand your evaluation path — are you looking to try hosted first via our PLG quickstart or go straight to a dedicated pilot or private deployment? And what are your success criteria.
[00:50] Leah: Ideally quickstart first, we want time-to-first-token fast — a dev should be able to spin up and call an endpoint same day. But for production we care about data residency and compliance, so dedicated or private might be needed.
[01:10] Omar: Also latency — we do user facing assistant features, so 200-300ms for short prompts would be sweet. Cost is a big factor too.
[01:25] Sasha: Totally — hosted is optimized for fastest time-to-first-token and we give free credits for initial tests. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, private gives VPC/on-prem for regulated data.
[01:40] Priya: Can you walk through the quickstart? specifically SDKs and auth — we have SSO via SAML, and need to provision service accounts for CI.
[01:55] Marco: Quickstart is usually: sign up, redeem free credits, get API key, drop one of our SDKs (python/js), and call the text-generation endpoint. We have sample apps — link in the deck. Auth supports token keys; for enterprise we support SAML/SSO provisioning and SCIM for user sync.
[02:20] Leah: How long until we can run a benchmark? I mean real prompts, not toy examples.
[02:30] Marco: You can run something basic within an hour with the SDK. For full benchmark with your prompt set, we'd recommend a small job — we can provide a runbook and scripts. With free credits you can cover initial runs.
[02:50] Sasha: We'll send the benchmark template and sample prompt harness after this call.
[03:00] Omar: About dedicated — what's the minimum commitment? We want to avoid overcommitting for a POC.
[03:12] Sasha: Dedicated is typically monthly reserved capacity; we do smaller pilot offerings — often a 3-month trial with reduced commit to validate throughput. Pricing tiers depend on GPU type and QPS.
[03:30] Priya: And private? We have some PHI-like data for a subset of customers — may require on-prem or VPC peering.
[03:42] Marco: Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments. We also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. There are additional compliance and deployment steps; our security team runs a checklist.
[04:00] Leah: Speaking of security, are you SOC2 and ISO? And can you share an audit log for inference requests?
[04:10] Sasha: Yes SOC2 Type II. We provide audit logs, retention options, RBAC, and can integrate with customer SIEMs. We'll share the security deck and the full questionnaire.
[04:25] Omar: How about model variants? If we need lower-latency cheaper models, can you route?
[04:33] Marco: Yes — smart routing lets you pick by latency/cost/region and we have model variants; also you can pin versions for rollouts. We also do KV cache & batching to improve unit cost.
[04:50] Leah: The team cares about quantization — do you support 8-bit or 4-bit runs for cost savings without large quality regressions?
[04:58] Marco: We have quantization profiles and the runtime picks kernels. For some models 4-bit is available and we've seen good cost reductions. We'll share model-specific guidance.
[05:15] Priya: On the PLG side — how much telemetry do you collect? We want minimal PII in logs for the quickstart.
[05:24] Sasha: Default hosted collects basic telemetry for usage/billing; we can mask inputs or disable retention for certain routes. For private deployments the customer controls logs.
[05:40] Leah: Great. Pricing question — do you charge per token or a blended QPS?
[05:48] Sasha: Hosted is usage-based (per-token; embeddings per unit). Dedicated is reserved capacity plus overage; pricing details I'll send. We'll include a cost model example for your workload.
[06:05] Omar: For the benchmark — can we test both hosted and a dedicated instance to compare latency/cost?
[06:12] Marco: Absolutely, we can spin up a short dedicated pilot and run the same harness to compare. We often do that for customers to show production economics.
[06:30] Leah: Any docs for quickstart? We want a reproducible guide for developers.
[06:36] Sasha: Link: https://redwood.ai/docs/quickstart — includes SDK samples, container examples, and a 'first token' tutorial. We'll also attach a one-pager.
[06:50] Priya: Ok send that. Also we use Okta — how fast is SSO setup for an evaluation?
[06:58] Marco: For evaluation you can create API keys, no SSO needed. For enterprise SSO with Okta it's usually a few days: we'll exchange metadata and we can enable SAML.
[07:15] Omar: Latency targets — we need p50 < 300ms for short prompts, p95 < 700ms. Is that realistic on hosted?
[07:25] Marco: For short prompts and smaller models yes, hosted data center proximate to your region should hit that; for stricter SLOs dedicated or pinned colocations are more predictable.
[07:45] Leah: What about data residency for EU customers? Can we pick regions?
[07:52] Sasha: Yes hosted offers region selection; for strict residency we recommend dedicated in-region or private deployment.
[08:05] Priya: Is there a sandbox environment for our devs?
[08:10] Sasha: Free credits cover sandbox usage; you can create multiple API keys per project.
[08:20] Omar: Are there rate limits on free credits?
[08:24] Marco: There are soft rate limits during onboarding to protect the service, but we can relax them for pilot runs.
[08:40] Leah: If we decide to go private later, how painful is migration of models and prompts?
[08:48] Marco: We support model versioning and packaging; migration is mostly about provisioning infra and transferring any private model weights if you bring your own. Prompts and prompt engineering transfer trivially.
[09:05] Sasha: Quick question to the group — what's your timeline for production?
[09:10] Leah: Ideally Q4, but we want a POC by end of July.
[09:18] Sasha: Ok that gives us time for pilot and benchmark in June/July.
[09:25] Priya: On integrations — we want KMS integration for encryption at-rest. Any limitations?
[09:32] Marco: We support customer-managed keys for private deployments and enterprise plans in hosted; we'll need details of your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) to scope.
[09:50] Omar: For the benchmark harness, can you take our dataset or do we run locally?
[09:56] Marco: Both options — you can run locally against hosted endpoints using your data redaction, or we can run in a controlled environment. For privacy, most customers run their data locally with our harness.
[10:10] Leah: Could you also speak to SLAs for Dedicated?
[10:16] Sasha: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency commitments depending on the tier. We'll include SLA details in the pricing doc.
[10:30] Marco: One more note: our runtime picks kernels and does batching automatically but you can tune batching and caching at route level for latency/cost tradeoffs.
[10:45] Priya: Great — can you share an example of cost per 1M tokens for a typical assistant workload?
[10:52] Sasha: We'll send cost examples; hard to generalize but the pricing sheet will show hosted vs dedicated per token and an estimated blended cost with batching.
[11:10] Omar: Any gotchas with dockerized apps calling the SDK behind corporate proxies?
[11:16] Marco: We have proxy-friendly SDKs; you might need to set env vars for proxy and token retrieval. We'll add a note in the quickstart.
[11:30] Leah: Final question — do you offer multi-tenant isolation if we host internal and customer-facing features?
[11:37] Sasha: Yes, we have route-level RBAC, per-project isolation, and can do dedicated pools per team for added isolation.
[11:50] Marco: Ok I can follow up with a technical appendix for your infra team.
[11:56] Priya: That'd be helpful.
[12:05] Sasha: Great, summary: we'll send pricing + credits, security deck, quickstart link, and benchmark runbook. Marco will own the technical appendix and runbook.
[12:20] Leah: Thanks, that works. We'll get Priya to share SSO/KMS details and Omar will pick a small prompt set for an initial run.
[12:35] Sasha: Awesome. We'll follow up with invites for the benchmark call.
[12:45] Omar: Thanks everyone.
[12:50] Sasha: Thanks all, talk soon.
[13:00] End of recording.
